english_verification.review_scope: Checked the current Mod's B14 opening identity, B48 formation conditions, representative Ravenmarch mission content, native English naming context, and fixed-revision Raven Banner/Ravenmarch Wiki chunks; not an exhaustive mission or event audit. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: The dedicated Ravenmarch Wiki page is an empty country frame and cannot certify detailed national history or current mechanics.
The Wiki and current scripts do not establish every later restoration or formation outcome described in older secondary material.
Current Mod names the Raven Banner ruler Jergan of Corveld, whereas the Wiki uses Captain Jherg of Corveld; retain the spelling difference.

rationale.colonization: The adventurer band must secure a foothold in Escann.
rationale.complexity: Formation prerequisites, regional projects, and event politics overlap.
rationale.dark_story: The vampire estate and masquerade duels create a distinctly dark thread.
rationale.difficulty: Formation and construction have gates; no hands-on difficulty test was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: Marcher and court-faction relations affect the choices.
rationale.early_pressure: The adventurer opening must contest land in the south.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Vampire politics and the religious court are supernatural in tone, but this is not a pure mage country.
rationale.narrative_density: The campaign has clear stages from an exiled adventurer band to a marcher court.
rationale.tall_play: Court management and marsh projects require sustained construction.
rationale.trade_economy: Southern and maritime trade routes are later development directions.
rationale.warfare: Both adventurer formation and southern restoration require war.

identity.appearance: Begins in 1444 as the Raven Banner B14 adventurer band and forms B48 after meeting the Escanni state-building conditions.
identity.formation_scope: The Raven Banner takes a foothold in Dostan's Way, Vernham, or Clovenwood, meets technology and peace conditions, then forms B48 and changes mission tree.

gaps.reason: No unambiguous tag/culture national idea definition found; no predecessor inference.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Beyond Corvuria our people have settled, exiled from our lands drowned by Daravan's Folly, into lands obscured by the fires of villages burning by countless orcs. By establishing our strongholds in lands shrouded between hill and dale, our fortresses are both difficult to find and highly defensible. It will take an enemy far above the average skill to find our lands.

description.text: On our voyage from Arca Corvur to Escann beyond, we encountered the ever-fabled Fey. As beautiful, and dangerous, as the legends say, we were tempted by the Fey to enter the Deepwoods proper and join them. Resolute in our mission, the Raven Banner ignored their charms, and set traps that night in case of retaliation. Later that night, that retaliation came, and Fey spirits attacked the camp. From then on the Raven Banner knew to always prepare for the enemy, and hurt them before they can ever harm you.

description.text:
The bravest and most noble of our soldiers swung great bludgeoning warhammers against the hordes of orcs. While they met great success in battle, reclaiming lands far from the heart of our new home, the age of heavy arms and armor soon came to an end with the ever-increasing use of firearms.

Veterans of these heavy infantry units assembled the Vernham Heavy Brigade, preserving their fighting style for future generations. However, their primary duty was to inspire courage and comradery amongst the greater army. Recruits were assigned to spar and wrestle with these great warriors. Although few could best them, all felt pride in themselves and gratitude for having the opportunity to improve their skills with these legends.

description.text:
The Raven Banner was established by Davan II síl Vivin of Corvuria in 1441 from the safety of Arca Corvur, to defeat the encroaching Greentide and claim lands for Corvuria. But in truth Jergan of Corveld, his fellow commanders, and their levied armies were exiles.

Frustrated by centuries of their lands ruined and drowned by the slow encroachment of Daravan's Folly, these nobles of the marshlands were a constant thorn to the monarch. Davan II saw an opportunity to be rid of this nuisance with the Greentide. The constant demands for supplies and funding to rebuild besoaked baronies, and intermittent rebellions from the lack of help, were too heavy a price to continue financing.

Jergan of Corveld, an eccentric but charismatic noble with dubious claims to the ruined city of Corveld, was summoned to Arca Corvur. Behind closed doors, the Raven Banner was established, outfitted with arms and supplies to drive deep into the Greentide. Eager to see them gone, and the deficit decrease, no binding agreements were made to ensure the loyalty of the Raven Banner to the holder of the Sapphire Key.

description.text:
All around us lie nations that threaten our way of life, ever on their mission to reclaim or pillage all of Escann. If they insist, the Ravenmarch will meet with fire and steel, and will stand victorious in the end.

Old Castanor has failed, crumbled, and burned into ashes. Once their lowly subject, Dostanor persists still despite the ruin of the Folly and bloodthirsty pretenders in Arca Corvur, but most of all in us. One day we will return, but for now Dostanor will be preserved in our hearths.

description.text:
Of all the gods of the Regent Court, Ryala of all has blessed our nation. Women and men both are fair, and true love is never heartbroken. The Sisterhood of Ryala's Smile upholds the tenets of Ryala in order to preserve our blessing, spreading the message of her smile even to beings such as orcs and goblins.

Ravenmarch was quickly swept up in the reformative spirit of the Corinite movement, remembering how they served with honor as the rear-guard of Corin's army. Their zealous hearts fixated on the role of Corin as a defender of the weak and a slayer of evil. But the old worship of Ryala and the death god Nerat did not wane in influence, and instead formed a triarchy of faith - life, war, and death.

description.text: Legends say that in Ravenmarch, it is best to be wary of windows, for it is said that the Lady with Dusken Hair watches and listens through them. Former spies, hunched over in taverns far from any window, tell in horror how one by one their comrades were found lifelessly discarded in the streets, completely drained of blood. Even the commoners tell tales of how their seditious neighbours or family members would be found dead and drained, displayed prominently in the town square. They say that this Lady is an ancient vampire, and others go so far as to say that the government of the Ravenmarch has recruited these unholy abominations as spies.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you only want rapid map-painting and do not want formation prerequisites or long marsh projects.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Seize a southern base as an adventurer band, form B48, build the march and court, manage vampire politics in the middle and late game, then push into Dostanor and farther afield.
player_overview.overview: Ravenmarch is not a ready-made kingdom in 1444. Lead the Raven Banner to a foothold in southern Escann, establish a frontier state, restore its marshes, manage the Triumvirate Court, and navigate the currents between knightly tradition and vampire nobility. It is both a restoration campaign aimed at Dostanor and a long story about turning broken land into a political centre.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Escanni adventurers, knightly restoration, court events, and frontier construction.
signature_features: An adventurer band forms into a country with a clear before-and-after campaign.
The Triumvirate Court and marsh restoration make religious politics and construction run through the campaign.
The vampire estate and masquerade events add a dark court narrative to knightly restoration.
player_overview.tagline: Build a southern march from a Corvurian adventurer band and make a knightly court stand amid marshes and vampire shadows.

reasons: A complete growth arc from adventurer band to kingdom.
Court and marsh governance give restoration a constructive dimension.
Vampire court events add narrative tension.
warnings: You must complete the Escanni formation prerequisites.
Court events and long construction are a poor fit for a pure rush strategy.

positive_indicators: Restoring marshes and improving the land.
Court politics provide adjustable institutional routes.
values.rationale: Frontier restoration and marsh management provide public benefits, while vampire court politics and religious-unification routes create risks of constraint and harm; conquest and monarchy are not treated as evidence of evil by themselves.
red_flags: The vampire estate and court-power struggles.
Some political events may endanger the ruler and social stability.
